look_here_first: Start with cane-like jointed culms from thick rhizomes, broad flat leaves, and the large terminal panicle. Inspect the ligule and mature spikelets to separate it from Phragmites; height alone is not a reliable key.

best_field_traits: Tall cane-like culms, commonly 2–6 m in the existing Kew-based review.
Thick rhizomes and broad flat leaves.
Large feathery terminal panicle, to about 70 cm; spikelets around 1 cm in the existing review.
morphology_keys.habit: Dense stands of tall cane-like stems; selected photograph shows a stand in Maui, not a Texas locality.
morphology_keys.leaves: Broad flat grass blades on conspicuous culms; sheath and ligule require close photographs.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Large terminal panicle; panicle architecture and spikelet detail remain photo gaps.
morphology_keys.lookalike_separators: Phragmites australis overlaps in tall reed habit; inspect ligule and mature spikelet/flower characters. Native and introduced Phragmites lineages need their own treatment; do not infer lineage or taxon from height or a distant stand photograph.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Check the reed's base and nodes before judging its height: thick rhizomes, robust cane-like jointed stems, broad flat leaves and a large terminal panicle suggest giant reed. Confirm by photographing the ligule and a mature spikelet; distant stand photos cannot separate it confidently from Phragmites.
crew_checkpoints: Photograph the rooted stand, stem diameter and leaf width with a scale; record whether thick rhizomes are visible without damaging a sensitive site.
At an intact leaf collar photograph sheath, ligule and blade junction at millimeter scale; do not infer ligule shape from a distant photo.
Collect a mature panicle branch only where permitted; photograph the entire panicle and individual spikelets with a millimeter ruler.
Compare with Phragmites australis using the same organ and magnification; neither tall height nor plume color alone proves identity.

look_alikes.check: Also forms tall reed stands; compare ligule and mature spikelet anatomy rather than height, and do not infer native versus introduced lineage from a photograph.
Can form tall colonies but has a different panicle/spikelet arrangement and narrower grass leaves; examine paired spikelets.
